title: Artificial Intelligence History
text: Artificial intelligence (AI) as a formal field was established at the Dartmouth Conference in 1956, organized by John McCarthy, Marvin Minsky, Nathaniel Rochester, and Claude Shannon. Early AI research focused on symbolic reasoning and expert systems. The field experienced periods of reduced funding and interest (AI winters) in the 1970s and 1980s when early optimism was not matched by results. The resurgence of neural networks in the 1980s–1990s, and the deep learning revolution starting around 2012, transformed AI capabilities. AlphaGo's defeat of world champion Go player Lee Sedol in 2016 marked a milestone. The release of large language models like GPT-4 and Claude in the 2020s sparked widespread public interest in AI.
